lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1673: one scanner per band, casts by the handful, and the menu stays open

Three things the owner reported in one message, all in the crafting screen.

A SCANNER YOU ALREADY CARRY IS NOT BUILDABLE AGAIN
"Once you build one and have one that's in the pouch, it should not be buildable
again." The rule reads a PROPERTY rather than naming the three scanners:
`effect.kind === 'scanner'` in exploration.json means an off-hand reader, one
slot, one band — a second copy cannot be equipped and reads nothing the first
does not. A hardcoded ['Pulse Scanner', 'Aetheric Scanner', 'Mud Scanner'] would
go stale the moment a fourth is authored, which is the shape of OTA-1603's
dog-armour kind drift.

It is per BAND, not per category: pulse reads Sentinel tech, aetheric reads
pre-flood phenomena, mud reads what the flood buried, so carrying all three is
the intended end state and owning one must never block building another. The
guard sits ABOVE the ingredient check, because "you already own this" is both
the better answer and the true one — otherwise the player is told they are short
3 Aether Crystal, which is not why the craft should stop. And it fails OPEN: a
catalog lookup that throws must never make a legitimate craft impossible.

+ / − AND MAX ON THE AETHERIC TAB, AND THE COUNT RIDES THE ACTION
The picker is the same NumberStepper BrandedModal already carries, so it is a
control the player has met. MAX is bounded by BOTH costs a shape has — one
aether fuel AND one Small Rock out of combat, since the shard is pulled from a
rock — because a MAX counting only fuel would promise casts that fizzle.

The count rides the action (`castCount`), it does not loop the verb. Looping
submitPlayerAction N times is exactly what OTA-1633 deleted: N parses, N Arbiter
remarks, N cognitive evals, N persists for one thumb tap. Each cast is still its
own d20 — batching must not turn ten rolls into one — so the loop sits around
the roll and its outcome instead.

⚠ THE STOP-TEST IS WHAT NEARLY SHIPPED WRONG, AND A PROBE CAUGHT IT
My first draft compared a fuel fingerprint before and after each pass and
stopped when nothing moved. It looked reasonable and it was not: a shape cast
with fuel but NO Small Rock still BURNS the fuel ("you shape the Aetherstone but
have no Small Rock to bind it to"), so the fingerprint moved, the loop ran on,
and asking for 5 casts with 3 rocks rolled FIVE times — spending two Aether
Residue on attempts that could not produce anything, and reporting nothing
wrong. Spending a player's materials silently on attempts that cannot succeed is
the exact class of defect this project keeps closing.

It now asks whether the NEXT cast can finish, stops there, and names what ran
out: "That is 3 of 5 — you're out of Small Rock to bind the shape to." A batch
that completes in full says nothing extra. ota1673 pins the preserved fuel, not
just the roll count — the count could be right while the fuel was spent anyway.

THE MENU STAYS OPEN
"Every time you do one it kicks you back out of crafting to the exploration
screen — you should be staying in crafting once you're done." The disciplines
were the last surface still calling setScreen('exploration'); an ordinary craft
has stayed put since OTA-983. The rolls still narrate into the world feed, so
nothing is lost by staying, and the same transient haul banner an ordinary craft
uses reports what came of it — from the same delta helper, so the two surfaces
cannot drift on "what did I just get".

- app/engine/oneToAPack.ts (new) — the property, the pack check, the refusal.
- app/state/aethercraftBatch.ts (new) — MAX_CAST_BATCH, the stop-test, the loop;
  its first draft sat inline in gameStore and tripped the OTA-1400 line ratchet,
  which is exactly what that ratchet is for.
- app/state/gameStore.ts — the guard on the craft door; MAX_CAST_BATCH;
  runAethercraft gains `times` with runAethercraftOnce underneath it, and
  aethercraftShortfall as the stop-test.
- app/screens/CraftingScreen.tsx — maxDisciplineCasts, the stepper, the banner,
  and the setScreen removed.
- __tests__/ota1673OneScannerPerBand.test.ts — 17 tests.
